intro: West Virginia runs its elections county by county, through each county clerk.

id_rule.text: Poll workers will ask for your ID when you check in. If you vote a provisional ballot because you did not show ID, take your ID to your county clerk's office before the canvass so your ballot can be counted. First-time voters may be asked for ID that shows their current address, such as a photo ID, utility bill, bank statement, government check, paycheck, or other government document.

dates.detail: You must register at least 21 days before the election to vote in it.

dates.label: Early voting
dates.detail: Vote early at the county courthouse, an annex, or another site your county sets, during normal business hours. Counties also hold hours from 9 am to 5 pm on the last two Saturdays. Sites and hours differ by county.

dates.label: Absentee ballot application deadline
dates.detail: Your county clerk must receive your application by this date, the 6th day before the election. You can send it by mail, fax, email, or in person.

dates.label: Last day to hand-deliver an absentee ballot
dates.detail: Deliver it to your county clerk's office by the day before Election Day. One person may not deliver more than two voters' ballots.

dates.label: Election Day
dates.detail: Polls are open 6:30 am to 7:30 pm. A mailed absentee ballot must be postmarked by Nov. 3. The state calendar lists Nov. 9 as the last day for those ballots to arrive.
